content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) has established specific target levels for hemoglobin A1C during pregnancy. Elevated A1C levels are associated with an increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes. For optimal results, the ADA recommends maintaining an A1C level of less than 6% (less than 42 mmol/mol). However, due to the accelerated turnover of red blood cells that occurs during pregnancy, adjustments to a target of less than 7% (less than 53 mmol/mol) may be necessary.
